# How-to: shell completions and human help (v26.9.16)

Your CLI should complete commands in bash/zsh/fish and show real `--help`
— without hand-writing either. Since v26.9.16 both are projections of the
same introspection manifest that powers `--introspect`: nouns as
subcommands, verbs per noun, option flags per verb.

## Generate completion scripts

```console
$ ./my_cli --completions bash
# completions for ex_noun_verb_cli -- generated by ex_noun_verb_cli --completions bash
_ex_noun_verb_cli_completions() { ... }
complete -F _ex_noun_verb_cli_completions ex_noun_verb_cli
```

`bash`, `zsh`, and `fish` are supported. Install by redirecting to the
right location, e.g.:

```console
$ ./my_cli --completions bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/my_cli
$ ./my_cli --completions zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_my_cli"
$ ./my_cli --completions fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/my_cli.fish
```

An unknown shell — or a known-but-unported one (`powershell`, `elvish`,
real policies in the upstream Rust project) — returns the typed
`invalid_option` error envelope naming the shell and the supported set,
exit 1. Never a fake script.

## Rename the completed command

Your binary usually is not called `ex_noun_verb_cli`. Set the name
completions attach to:

```elixir
config :ex_noun_verb_cli, completion_command: "my_cli"
```

## Human help

```console
$ ./my_cli --help          # usage + every noun's command table
$ ./my_cli --help calc     # one noun only
```

The table lists each verb with its doc string, options with types and
required markers, positional names, and a chaining quick reference —
every word of it implied by the manifest (a falsifier in the v26.9.16
ARD: help text the manifest does not imply cannot exist).

## The shell policy table

`ExNounVerbCli.Shell` ports upstream `clap_noun_verb`'s `ShellType`
policies (which shells are supported, which support command substitution
in completion functions, line endings — powershell is `\r\n`). The
completion generator reads this table; nothing guesses.
